extracted.intended_audience: students, scholars, and policymakers interested in colonial administration, political theory, and representative government
extracted.subtask_description: Extract principles and evaluative criteria for governing colonies and dependencies, including who should govern, how authority should be organized, and what safeguards and practices produce good administration. Focuses on distinctions between self-governing colonies and backward dependencies and on administrative recruitment, responsibility, and imperial obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full internal self-government for European-race colonies
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a fixed principle of the policy of Great Britain... that her colonies of European race, equally with the parent country, possess the fullest measure of internal self-government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colonies should be allowed to make their own free representative constitutions and alter previously given constitutions; each governed by its own legislature and executive on highly democratic principles; the crown/Parliament veto is nominal and rarely exercised except on imperial questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberal distinction between imperial and colonial questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The veto of the crown and of Parliament... is only exercised (and that very rarely) on questions which concern the empire, and not solely the particular colony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical liberal construction shown by allowing colonies disposal of unappropriated lands; imperial powers should be narrowly used so as not to intrude on local affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colonial fiscal sovereignty (taxation powers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each [colony] is free even to tax at its pleasure the commodities imported from the mother country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colonies have wide fiscal autonomy—wider than U.S. states—affecting trade relations and internal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition that union is an unequal federation
rubrics_metrics.description: Their union with Great Britain is the slightest kind of federal union; but not a strictly equal federation, the mother country retaining to itself the powers of a federal government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This inequality disadvantages dependencies because they have no voice in foreign policy and can be compelled to enter wars without prior consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit contributions of colonists to imperial wars
rubrics_metrics.description: In all wars, save those which... are incurred for the sake of the particular colony, the colonists should not (without their own voluntary request) be called on to contribute any thing to the expense except what may be required for the specific local defense of their ports, shores, and frontiers against invasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since the mother country may expose colonies to risk by its foreign policy, it is just that she undertakes a considerable portion of the cost of their military defense, at least the standing army cost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open imperial service to colonial inhabitants on equal terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Open the service of government in all its departments, and in every part of the empire, on perfectly equal terms, to the inhabitants of the colonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making all offices and dignities freely open to colonial natives (examples: Guernsey/Jersey) counteracts disloyalty and grievances and supplies an equivalent to loss of sovereignty by offering career and honor in the imperial system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimacy of direct rule for backward populations if transitional
rubrics_metrics.description: There are others [dependencies] which have not attained that state, and which, if held at all, must be governed by the dominant country, or by persons delegated for that purpose by it... if it is the one which in the existing state of civilization of the subject people most facilitates their transition to a higher stage of improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct governance can be legitimate where it best promotes the governed people's advancement; choice of mode should be judged by its facilitation of improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable aim of civilized rule: supply the best possible despotism
rubrics_metrics.description: The ruling country ought to be able to do for its subjects all that could be done by a succession of absolute monarchs, guaranteed by irresistible force... and qualified by their genius to anticipate all that experience has taught to the more advanced nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an ideal to aim for when ruling 'barbarous or semi-barbarous' peoples: to make rule a good rather than an evil, even if the ideal is rarely fully realized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing under responsibility to a distant people is effectively despotism
rubrics_metrics.description: To govern a country under responsibility to the people of that country, and to govern one country under responsibility to the people of another, are two very different things... the last is despotism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A minister accountable to the home public (not the subject people) will inevitably promote home interests and misunderstand local needs; distant accountability tends to produce worse outcomes than local rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign rulers lack native knowledge and instinct
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreigners do not feel with the people. They can not judge... how it will affect the feelings or appear to the minds of the subject population. The laws, the customs, the social relations... are all strange to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign administrators must learn slowly and imperfectly; they depend on natives for information and may mistrust whom to trust—this requires exceptionally capable administrators and careful organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home opinion can misdirect benevolent reforms (cultural insensitivity risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: What makes the excellence of the first is, that freedom is preferable to despotism... but the opinion of the dominant country tends to act more injuriously than beneficially... demand for having the Bible taught... in government schools... to Asiatic eyes it is quite another thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures that seem just from European viewpoint (e.g., religious instruction) may be perceived as proselytism and undermine government safety; caution about imposing home cultural norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: European settlers are a frequent source of oppression and misgovernance
rubrics_metrics.description: English settlers... are of all others those who most need to be held under powerful restraint... they think the people of the country mere dirt under their feet... the simplest act of protection to the inhabitants... they denounce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Settlers have local power and home influence; governments must guard against settler abuses as settlers can sway home opinion and pressure authorities to abandon protections for natives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home advocacy tends to favor local elites over masses
rubrics_metrics.description: In the subject community also there are oppressors and oppressed... the former, not the latter, who have the means of access to the English public... The silent myriads obtain none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interventions driven by elite interests in the subject country produce biased outcomes; policymakers must recognize which local actors have access to home channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibility to the governed is the chief security for good government
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsibility to the governed is the greatest of all securities for good government; responsibility to somebody else not only has no such tendency, but is as likely to produce evil as good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local accountability produces better governance; delegating responsibility to a body whose duty is only to the governed helps secure better administration than accountability to a distant populace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use publicity and parliamentary discussion sensibly
rubrics_metrics.description: The responsibility of the British rulers of India to the British nation is chiefly useful because, when any acts of the government are called in question, it insures publicity and discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicity allows informed individuals to weigh in; even if majority lack understanding, a few knowledgeable opinions can correct abuses—public oversight is useful but not a substitute for proper local accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide good rulers rather than attempt direct rule from home
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not by attempting to rule directly a country like India, but by giving it good rulers, that the English people can do their duty to that country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than micromanaging from home, the metropolitan power should supply competent, permanent administrators focused on local governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Govern through a delegated, comparatively permanent body
rubrics_metrics.description: The only mode which has any chance of tolerable success is to govern through a delegated body of a comparatively permanent character, allowing only a right of inspection and a negative voice to the changeable administration of the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An intermediate body, composed of persons who have professional knowledge and local experience, is less subject to home political swings and better identifies with the governed people's interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegated administration should have duty only to the governed
rubrics_metrics.description: A delegated administration has always this advantage over a direct one, that it has, at all events, no duty to perform except to the governed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a body can be kept free of profit motives from misgovernment and of bias from other class interests; it serves as the dependency's advocate before imperial authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep key appointments out of party patronage and jobbing
rubrics_metrics.description: To put this one class of appointments as far as possible out of harm's way is of more consequence than the worst which can happen to all other offices in the state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preventing appointment by patronage avoids incompetence and corruption in positions that determine the character of dependency administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruit and train administrators via promotion from lower ranks and exams
rubrics_metrics.description: The safety of the country is, that those by whom it is administered be sent out in youth, as candidates only, to begin at the bottom of the ladder, and ascend higher or not, as, after a proper interval, they are proved qualified... competitive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A civil service system that recruits by competitive exam and promotes by merit forms the necessary professional class of administrators; opening higher posts to outsiders invites patronage and decline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve the highest executive appointment as an exception (Viceroy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The only excepted appointment should be the highest one of all. The Viceroy of British India should be a person selected from all Englishmen for his great general capacity for government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The supreme ruler should be exempt from service-class prejudices; there are reasons why the viceroy should not be a member of the regular service so as to retain impartiality and general capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal qualities of agents are decisive
rubrics_metrics.description: In a country like India, every thing depends on the personal qualities and capacities of the agents of government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The system must be calculated to form fit persons; appointment by convenience or patronage will cause decline and fall of rule—hence emphasis on training, selection, and permanent career development.
